FXUS62 KMFL 051744
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
1244 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

...New UPDATE...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1240 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

  - Minor coastal flooding expected during times of high tide.

  - Elevated risk of rip currents today for the Palm Beaches.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 1240 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

Latest RRFS run continues to show the possibility of a few showers
later this afternoon into early this evening over Mainland Monroe
and the Everglades, so painted some slight chance PoPs over there
for a few hours. Otherwise, the forecast remains largely on track. 

Did extend the Coastal Flood Statement for the Atlantic coast
through early Friday evening for minor flooding around the high
tide cycles. Additional coastal flood headlines will eventually be
needed for the weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 313 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

A much different weather scenario is now developing across SoFlo 
with mid-lvl drier air now filtering into the region. A large 
trough/low system is migrating eastward across the SE CONUS, and 
will keep the best associated dynamic support well to the north of 
SoFlo today and Friday. CAPE/instability parameters seem to get 
highly suppressed across the region as strong sfc high pressure 
builds in the wake of a frontal passage. Ensembles and NBM Wx/POPs 
coverage drops into the 10 percent range for each afternoon, with
mainly warm and mostly sunny conditions prevailing. This is a 
much welcomed change from previous days, which will help those 
communities still struggling with flooded roads and lingering 
water. 

Pressure gradients have also relaxed across the area, with winds 
becoming generally light and variable through the morning hours, 
then ENE in the 5-10kt range this afternoon. 

Increased daytime heating and decreased cloud cover will result in 
afternoon highs reaching the mid to upper 80s each day. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 313 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

Latest long range model solutions remain in fair agreement about 
reinforcing high pressure and drier conditions prevailing across the 
region during the weekend in the wake of a dry FROPA. Forecast 
POPs/Wx coverage remain around single-digits each day through 
Sunday. Then for early next week, models depict a potential mid-lvl 
trough moving across the area and bringing increasing chances of 
showers for the late Monday-Tuesday timeframe. But even so, max POPs 
seem to remain in the 20-30% range. 

The latest trend in guidance is also to bring a more pronounced 
temperature gradient as overall northerly flow develops in the wake 
of the FROPA. Afternoon highs should remain in the upper 70s to low 
80s by early next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1222 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

Mainly VFR conditions expected today. Light NE winds through the
early evening with a brief NNW wind expected at APF. Light and
variable winds overnight.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Marine conditions will continue to gradually improve across the 
Atlantic waters as winds subside, and a more gentle NE flow 
develops. A few marine showers may develop today, but weather 
conditions should remain generally dry over the marine zones. 
Significantly drier conditions will prevail through the upcoming 
weekend. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

As onshore flow weakens, the Risk for Rip Currents across 
the Palm Beach waters will decrease to moderate today. Higher 
than usual tides will also continue to keep elevated water levels 
near the coast today. 

&&

ABNT20 KNHC 051755
TWOAT 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
100 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Western and Central Atlantic:
A gale-force, non-tropical low pressure area located a few hundred 
miles south of Bermuda is producing disorganized convection to the 
north and east of its center. Environmental conditions could allow 
this system to gradually acquire some subtropical characteristics 
during the next couple of days or so while it moves slowly eastward 
over the western and central subtropical Atlantic. By late this 
weekend, upper-level winds are forecast to become unfavorable for 
further development of this system. A new non-tropical low could 
form to its east this weekend. Although environmental conditions are 
unlikely to support significant subtropical or tropical development 
of that system, gale-force winds are possible over parts of the 
central subtropical Atlantic through the weekend. For more 
information, including Gale Warnings, please see High Seas Forecasts 
issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
Forecaster Reinhart
